reviewer_notes: Gate entries are defensible as source-side protocol support factors, not as physical amplitudes or likelihood weights. Keep the caveat that each numeric gate remains a review ledger value and must not be inferred from endpoint performance.

KiDS/COSEBIs low-mode may retain positive source-side support because the endpoint/source route is frozen and the structured low-tail signal is recorded, but tomographic and operator-level blockers prevent validation-facing promotion.

Observer/path low-z support is defensible only as narrow source-side support for the already frozen 12-object permission-replay route. It is not population validation and should not be upweighted without source-native path/metric/environment support.

DESI shape/readout support is defensible as a narrow positive-support channel after the source synthesis and permission-only route, but the small margin and row sensitivity must remain explicit caveats.

Zero-support branches are correctly excluded from positive joint support under the current ledgers: ACT Kpath is control-dominated, time/clock is control-limited, void/web and distance-shell proxies are weak or negative, and sky-z remains diagnostic/control.

The equal alpha_a=1/7 rule is acceptable as a frozen preflight default because it is residual-blind and hard-gate preserving, but a validation-facing endpoint should freeze a source-reviewed exponent vector before scoring.

No promotion from protocol support Q_i to validation-facing source support is allowed before a separate covariance-aware joint likelihood or likelihood surrogate with shuffled-channel, wrong-channel, sign-flip, block-drop, and null/readout controls exists.
